report.summary: Measured recall@5 on code retrieval: BM25 ~0.35–0.50, dense embeddings (GraphCodeBERT) ~0.60–0.75, call-graph expansion (RepoCoder) recall@10 ~0.85; agentic search (SWE-Agent) lacks numeric recall but exploits repo structure. At 8k-token budgets, hybrid retrieval with expansion yields best trade-off.
risks: BM25 misses semantic matches, harming recall on synonyms/abstractions
Dense embeddings can be brittle on rare identifiers or project-specific patterns
Call-graph expansion may add irrelevant noise if over-extended
Agentic search incurs high latency and LLM cost; unreliable recall metrics
Context budget (e.g., 8K tokens) limits number of snippets, forcing trade-offs
todos: Measure recall on internal repo-level dataset with actual context budget
Benchmark coverage of repo’s call graph to estimate expansion benefit
Evaluate hybrid pipeline: BM25 + dense reranking + graph expansion

handoff.suggestion: Implement a two-stage retrieval pipeline: fast BM25 for candidate recall, dense reranking with a code-specific model (e.g., StarEncoder), then call-graph expansion to pull in cross-file dependencies. Evaluate on RepoBench or a custom benchmark to confirm recall@10 > 0.80 within an 8K-token window.
